COURT’S OR JUDGES’S ORDERS
22.11.2023 CRLR No. 851 of 2023
Hon’ble Alok Kumar Verma, J.
Revisionists have filed the present 
Revision to enhance the monthly allowance 
granted under Section 125 of the Code of 
Criminal Procedure, 1973 by the learned 
Judge, Family Court, Vikas Nagar, District 
Dehradun on 16.08.2023 in Miscellaneous 
Criminal Case No. 87 of 2021 and for 
maintenance allowance of the revisionist no. 
1-wife of respondent no. 2-opposite party. 
The learned Judge, Family Court, Vikas 
Nagar, District Dehradun has directed the 
revisionist no. 2 to pay Rs. 8,000/- per month 
to his minor son for his maintenance, while, 
the said Application, filed under Section 125 
of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973 has 
been rejected in relation to revisionist no. 1-
wife of the respondent no. 2. 
2. Heard Mr. Rajat Mittal, learned counsel 
for the revisionists and Mr. Akshay Latwal, 
learned Brief Holder for the State. 
3. Mr. Rajat Mittal, Advocate, submits that 
the respondent no. 2, husband of revisionist 
no. 1 got solemnized second marriage. 
4. Admit. 
5. Issue notice to the respondent no. 2. 
6. Steps to be taken within a week. 
7. List on 29.12.2023.
 (Alok Kumar Verma, J.)
 22.11.2023
Shiksha

COURT’S OR JUDGES’S ORDERS
CRLR No. 851 of 2023
Hon’ble Rakesh Thapliyal, J.
1. Ms. Garima Thapa, learned counsel for the 
revisionist. 
2. Mr. Tumul Nainwal, learned AGA for the State. 
3. Mr. Amit Kapri, learned counsel for the 
respondent.
4. Parties are present along with their minor son. 
Revisionist wife apprise to this Court that respondent 
husband married with another lady and living with 
her. She has also shown some photographs and for half 
an hour, this Court interacted with the parties but 
respondent husband is repeatedly making statement 
that all these photographs are fake. Not only, he also 
submits that the photographs enclosed at page nos. 90, 
91, 92 and 93, are also fake. 
5. This Court post the matter at 04.00 p.m. so that he 
may go through with photographs. 
6. Now, after post lunch session, respondent 
husband submits that he was under depression pre 
lunch session and could not understand the query of 
the Court and all these photographs are genuine. This 
Court further interacted with him by putting certain 
more queries but what this Court observed that 
respondent husband is repeatedly misleading to the 
Court by giving false statement. This is really a very 
serious issue. 
7. Be that as it may, taking into consideration that 
there is a matrimonial dispute in between the parties 
and the respondent husband is now married with 
another lady, now the question is in such an 
eventuality what further steps can be taken to secure 
future of wife and son. 
8. Learned counsel for the revisionist submits that 
respondent husband married with another lady during 
the divorce proceeding and is running a jewellery shop 
and he has transferred a house in the name of lady with 
whom he married. He has another shop in Vikas 
Nagar. 
9. This Court is giving three days time to the  respondent husband to give complete details of his 
properties including bank account, ITR of last five 
years and account statement of the lady with whom he 
married. 
10. On the next date, respondent husband shall 
remain present in the Court. 
11. List on 08.04.2026 as a first case.
 (Rakesh Thapliyal, J.)
 02.04.2026
SKS

COURT’S OR JUDGE’S ORDERS
CRLR No. 851 of 2023
Hon'ble Rakesh Thapliyal, J.
1. Ms. Garima Thapa, learned counsel for 
the revisionist.
2. Mr. B.C. Joshi, learned A.G.A for the 
State.
3. Mr. Amit Kapri, learned counsel for the 
respondent.
4. The respondent Jitendra Singh, the 
husband of revisionist no.1 married with 
another lady though divorce decree is 
already stayed by this Court. The revisionist 
no. 2 is the minor son. Earlier the 
respondent denied in open court about the 
second marriage and submits that all the 
photographs as shown by the revisionist are 
fake but subsequently post lunch session, he 
tendered apology and submitted that he was 
in depression and all these photographs with 
regard to the second marriage are genuine. 
He was directed to file the details of the 
assets including the ITR along with the 
account statement of the second wife. 
5. It appears that the respondent no. 2 is 
repeatedly misleading to the court and have 
not approach with clean hands since he is 
not disclosing about details of the assets.
Learned counsel for the revisionist submits 
that recently the respondent has transferred  the property in the name of second wife on 
06.09.2023 and on 24.03.2026 the another 
property was sold out. Not only this, even 
prior to that one property was purchased by 
him at the cost of Rs. 40,000,00/-. The 
counsel for the revisionist also pointed out 
that as per the ITR the revisionist is doing 
some business but he is giving the 
impression to the court that he is working as 
an Assistant in a jewelry shop. She also 
pointed out that the jewelry shop is owned 
by respondent no.2.
6. This Court is of the view that the 
respondent no.2 is repeatedly misleading to 
the Court but before taking further steps 
this Court is of the view that let the S.H.O. 
concerned may get the details of all assets 
of the respondent no. 2 as well as his 
second wife and submit the report before 
this Court and he can take assistance of 
some income tax officer. The report shall be 
placed before this Court within two weeks.
7. List this case on 27.04.2026. 
(Rakesh Thapliyal, J.) 
08.04.2026
